The appeal path, quoted from POL-GEN-04

Every ruling issued without human review is a provisional ruling. Either party may appeal it once, within 30 days of the trip or of the ruling's issue, whichever is later, by lodging the appeal with the platform's help channel. An appeal (a) is heard by a human reviewer who did not take part in any earlier review of the same trip; (b) may add only record-type evidence - a GPS export, a fare or payment statement, an ERP gantry record with gantry name, entry time and cashcard statement, a call log, a photograph with its capture time - and may not add or amend a party statement; (c) suspends execution of any amount not yet executed and freezes it until decided, and where the amount was executed under POL-GEN-05 before the appeal, a successful appeal reverses it; (d) may not be withdrawn and re-lodged. A second appeal on the same trip, an appeal lodged after 30 days, or an appeal that adds only statements is refused. The appeal decision is recorded as a human closure under POL-GEN-06, enters the precedent store, and is final on the platform. This clause licenses no ruling value: an appeal is a route to human review, not a ruling, and it is lodged after a ruling has issued.

POL-GEN-05: the monetary effect is SGD 13.70 against an execution threshold of SGD 8.00. It exceeds the threshold, so the amount is issued but not executed: it is held for release and the case is placed in the human queue.

The judge's explanation, as written

Short version: the route deviation is real and established, no excuse for it survives on this record, and the fare arithmetic gives the rider SGD 13.70 back out of the SGD 58.10 charged. THE DEVIATION. POL-RD-01 makes the GPS trace the governing measurement, and the trace records 23.97 km between the recorded pickup and dropoff. Optimum is 18.0 km, so the excess is 5.97 km, or 33.2% of optimal. Both establishment tests are met (above 20% and above 0.8 km), so the deviation is ESTABLISHED. It is not a MATERIAL deviation — it is under both the 50% and 8.0 km gates — so POL-RD-06 does not engage. To the rider: the 24.0 km on the trip record is a rounded copy and the trace's 23.97 km is used; your 'extra 6 km' is a slight overstatement, and the measured excess is 5.97 km. NO EXONERATION. To the driver: your congestion account cannot be run under POL-RD-03, because that clause needs a traffic_advisory naming a road the optimal route uses with a validity window covering the trip, and the only advisory artifact in the bundle, EV-ADVIS-00114-01, is MISSING with weight 0.0 and no payload. Under POL-RD-13 the assertion is tested against that advisory and nothing else, so it carries no weight under POL-RD-08 and neither reduces the 5.97 km nor supplies an amended optimal route. Your in-app message at 18:59:20 ('AYE jam boss, this way faster') records only that you chose to leave the optimal corridor; your counterparty statement that there was 'No advisory that I know of' is consistent with that. Because you named no advisory evidence ID, POL-RD-13(1) makes the absent artifact a gap in the bundle rather than an exculpatory clause invoked against a cited artifact, so POL-RD-10(5) is not engaged and this case is ruleable now rather than held. For completeness: tracing speed against a jam is not a substitute for the advisory the clause requires. To the rider: POL-RD-04 does not apply either. Your message at 18:58:40 ('adam road?? jurong is the other way') is a challenge, not an instruction to detour, and no chat message carries a waypoint_hint, so no distance is excluded from the excess on that ground. Neither side gets an adjusted optimal: the booked 18.0 km stands. THE REFUND (POL-RD-02, METERED fare on EV-FARE-00114). recomputed_fare = ((3.80 base + 0.75 x 18.0 km + 0.28 x 30.0 min) x 1.6 surge) + 0.80 platform fee + 2.50 ERP on the optimal route = (25.70 x 1.6) + 3.30 = 41.12 + 3.30 = 44.42. Refund = 58.10 charged_total - 44.42 = 13.68, rounded up to the nearest SGD 0.05 on the payable figure = SGD 13.70. The 1.6 surge is read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier and is preserved on both sides of the equation; the surge you accepted is not refunded, only the distance and time over the excess. ERP. Of the 4.50 charged, 2.50 is the Kim Keat Link gantry on the optimal route and stays inside the recomputed fare. The 2.00 Adam Road gantry is off the optimal route but is a genuine crossing — the trace passes 8.76 m from it — so it is not a phantom line and no billing-integrity referral arises. Under POL-RD-09(1) it is already comprehended in the 13.70 and must not be added on top of it. OUTCOME. PARTIAL_REFUND of SGD 13.70 to the rider; no driver compensation. 13.70 is above the SGD 0.50 de minimis and well under the 90% of charged_total that would make it a full refund. No referral fires: no material deviation, no repeat-pattern threshold (deviation_flags_90d is 1 across 412 completed 90-day trips, under both the count and ratio gates), and no unmatched charge line. Confidence is 0.9; the facts the ruling rests on — the trace measurement, the booked optimal and the fare lines — all sit on weight-1.0 artifacts, and the missing advisory carries no fact and does not cap the ruling. The monetary effect (13.70) exceeds the SGD 8.00 automatic-execution threshold, so the amount is issued but held for human release under POL-GEN-05. The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).

What each side argued

The rider advocate

kept The trip's own GPS polyline measures 23.97 km between the recorded pickup and the recorded dropoff, against a booked optimal of 18.0 km — an excess of 5.97 km, or 33.17% of optimal. Both POL-RD-01 establishment tests are passed with room to spare: the excess is greater than 20% of optimal_distance_km and greater than 0.8 km in absolute terms. The route deviation is established on this trip's own trace.

evidence EV-GPS-00114, EV-TRIP-00114 · clauses POL-RD-01

kept The trace figure governs the measurement. POL-RD-01 requires gps_trace.trace_distance_km to be used for the threshold test and forbids citing trip_record.actual_distance_km, which is only a rounded convenience copy of the same measurement. I therefore rely on the trace's 23.97 km; even the rounded 24.0 km copy would give an excess of about 6 km, so the tests pass on either figure and nothing turns on the discrepancy.

evidence EV-GPS-00114, EV-TRIP-00114 · clauses POL-RD-01

kept The rider has carried the initial burden under POL-RD-08. Limb (a): trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown all carry the identifier TRP-00114 and describe the same 18:40-19:20 movement. Limb (b): the excess of 5.97 km is measured from an entirely unimpaired trace, so no independent corroboration is required. The rider's enhanced-corroboration trigger also does not fire — rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 1, well below the threshold of 4, and may not be used to deny a claim that is otherwise proven.

evidence EV-TRIP-00114, EV-GPS-00114, EV-FARE-00114, EV-RPROF-00114 · clauses POL-RD-08

kept The driver's explanation is a traffic assertion he ties to no artifact, and the bundle contains no advisory at all. I cite the absence itself: EV-ADVIS-00114-01 is MISSING, carries weight 0.0 and no payload, and its blocking issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT records that no LTA advisory covers the AYE, the PIE or the Alexandra corridor in the 18:36-19:20 window. The driver's own in-app reply names no advisory, and his counterparty statement concedes 'No advisory that I know of'. Under POL-RD-13 the external-cause assertion is tested against the traffic_advisory for this trip and nothing else; that comparison cannot be run, and the assertion carries no weight under POL-RD-08. I disclose the artifact's 0.0 weight and MISSING_ARTIFACT status expressly.

evidence EV-ADVIS-00114-01, EV-CHAT-00114 · clauses POL-RD-13, POL-RD-08

discarded POL-RD-03 exoneration is unavailable and no closure-adjusted optimal exists. The clause requires a traffic_advisory naming a road or segment the optimal route traverses with a validity window overlapping the trip, and the only advisory artifact in the bundle is MISSING at weight 0.0. Without it there is no shortest_lawful_alternative_km, no justified_excess_km and no adjusted duration, so the booked optimal of 18.0 km stands as the baseline against which the 23.97 km trace is measured.

evidence EV-ADVIS-00114-01, EV-TRIP-00114 · clauses POL-RD-03

Discarded by the referee (IMPAIRMENT_UNDISCLOSED): the claim cites impaired artifact EV-ADVIS-00114-01 at weight_multiplier 0.0 but does not name its issue code(s): MISSING_ARTIFACT

kept The detour was not rider-requested. POL-RD-04 requires a rider instruction in the chat_log, and the only message from the rider is a challenge to the route — 'adam road?? jurong is the other way', sent 18:58:40 — which is a question, not an instruction, and which was sent after the vehicle had already left the optimal corridor. derived.waypoint_approach.messages is empty and no chat message carries a waypoint_hint, so the 200 m corroboration test of POL-RD-04 cannot be run and no distance is excluded from the excess on this ground.

evidence EV-CHAT-00114, EV-GPS-00114 · clauses POL-RD-04

kept What the chat log does establish is that the driver elected the corridor himself. His message at 18:59:20 — 'AYE jam boss, this way faster' — is both an admission that he deliberately chose to leave the optimal route and a bare congestion claim resting on no advisory. Under POL-RD-13 limb (2), where the rider has shown an excess meeting the POL-RD-01 threshold on a trace that is not impaired, the deviation stands at the measured figure and POL-RD-02 runs against the booked optimal route; the driver's traffic assertion neither reduces the excess nor supplies an amended optimal, and the ruling should record that it was discarded and that no advisory was on file.

evidence EV-CHAT-00114, EV-GPS-00114, EV-TRIP-00114 · clauses POL-RD-13, POL-RD-02

kept The refund is arithmetic, not discretionary. The fare model on EV-FARE-00114 is METERED, and the surge multiplier of 1.6 is read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier on that same artifact — the multiplier lives there and nowhere else, and the rider does not contest it. recomputed_fare = ((3.80 base + 0.75 x 18.0 optimal km + 0.28 x 30.0 optimal min) x 1.6 surge) + 0.80 platform fee + 2.50 ERP on the optimal route = 44.42. Refund = 58.10 charged_total - 44.42 = 13.68, rounded up on the payable figure to the nearest SGD 0.05, giving 13.70.

evidence EV-FARE-00114, EV-TRIP-00114 · clauses POL-RD-02

kept On the ERP lines: of the 4.50 charged, 2.50 is the Kim Keat Link towards Tuas gantry, which lies on the optimal route and properly stays inside the recomputed fare, and 2.00 is the Adam Rd towards Tuas gantry, which the optimal route does not use. The trace passes 8.76 m from that gantry, so it is a real crossing and not a phantom line. Under POL-RD-09(1) that off-route 2.00 is already comprehended in the POL-RD-02 refund, because the recomputed fare includes only on-optimal-route gantries; it is itemised for transparency but must not be added on top of the 13.70.

evidence EV-FARE-00114, EV-GPS-00114 · clauses POL-RD-09

kept No POL-RD-10 escalation trigger fires, so this case is ruleable now. The trace is unbroken — 241 fixes at a 10 s sampling interval, 100% coverage, max_gap_sec 0.0 — so it is not impaired under POL-RD-07(a) to (c) and POL-RD-10(3) cannot apply. The trip identifiers match across trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown; no timestamp runs backwards or disagrees by more than 10 minutes; every charge line has a counterpart in the trace; and because the driver cites no advisory identifier, an absent advisory he never invoked is a gap in the bundle, not an exculpatory clause invoked against a cited artifact within POL-RD-10(5).

evidence EV-GPS-00114, EV-TRIP-00114, EV-FARE-00114 · clauses POL-RD-10, POL-RD-07

kept The remedy follows from the arithmetic: a refund of 13.70 is well above the SGD 0.50 de minimis, so NO_ACTION is excluded, and it is only 23.5% of charged_total, below the 90% share that would convert it into a full refund. The correct outcome for the filing rider is a partial refund of 13.70 against the contested charge of 15.00, with the off-route ERP accounted for inside that figure rather than on top of it.

evidence EV-FARE-00114 · clauses POL-RD-02

The driver advocate

kept On this trip's governing trace the excess is 5.97 km over an 18.0 km optimal route — 33.17% — which clears the POL-RD-01 establishment gates (greater than 20% and greater than 0.8 km) but falls far short of the 50% and 8.0 km materiality gates. The deviation is therefore ESTABLISHED but NOT MATERIAL: POL-RD-06 is not engaged, there is no established pattern to uplift the remedy to FULL_REFUND, and no driver-conduct referral arises. The most the rider can be awarded on this record is the POL-RD-02 arithmetic.

evidence EV-GPS-00114, EV-TRIP-00114 · clauses POL-RD-01, POL-RD-06

kept POL-RD-01 makes gps_trace.trace_distance_km the governing measurement of actual distance and forbids citing the trip record's rounded copy for the threshold test. The trace records 23.97 km, not the 24.0 km convenience figure on the trip record, so the rider's round-trip characterisation of an 'extra 6 km' overstates the measured excess, which is 5.97 km against an optimal of 18.0 km.

evidence EV-GPS-00114, EV-TRIP-00114 · clauses POL-RD-01

kept No repeat-deviation pattern may be found against this driver on the only two fields POL-RD-06 and POL-GEN-01 permit: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 1, which is below the threshold of 3, and 1 divided by driver_profile.completed_trips_90d of 412 is 0.0024, far below the 0.05 ratio. The lifetime counter prior_deviation_flags (2) is a near-synonym of the trailing-90-day field and is context only; it may not be substituted for the field the clause names.

evidence EV-DPROF-00114 · clauses POL-RD-06, POL-GEN-01

kept The refund is capped by the POL-RD-02 arithmetic and the off-route ERP may not be added on top of it. The recomputed fare is ((3.80 + 0.75 x 18.0 + 0.28 x 30.0) x 1.6) + 0.80 + 2.50, the 2.50 being the only gantry lying on the optimal route (PIE Kim Keat Link towards Tuas, on_optimal_route true), giving 44.42; the refund is 58.10 - 44.42 = 13.68, payable 13.70. The Adam Road gantry's 2.00 is already comprehended in that figure under POL-RD-09(1) and must never be added again, and the 1.6 surge recorded on the fare_breakdown is preserved on both sides of the equation and is not refundable distance or time. The 15.00 contested at filing exceeds what the policy arithmetic supports.

evidence EV-FARE-00114 · clauses POL-RD-02, POL-RD-09

kept Both billed gantries were genuinely crossed: the trace's nearest fix is 0.0 m from the Kim Keat Link gantry and 8.76 m from the Adam Road gantry, both well inside the 250 m match radius POL-RD-09 uses, so neither line is a phantom charge and no billing-integrity refund or referral under POL-RD-09(4) arises. The same trace fixes show the driver ran through the on-optimal-route Kim Keat Link gantry on the first leg, so the deviation is confined to a single later segment and is not a wholesale disregard of the booked corridor; the excess is bounded at the 5.97 km measured.

evidence EV-GPS-00114, EV-FARE-00114 · clauses POL-RD-09, POL-RD-01

kept The bundle's only traffic_advisory for this trip is MISSING — issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, weight_multiplier 0.0, disclosed here under POL-GEN-02. POL-RD-03 therefore cannot be run and the driver does not press congestion as exoneration; but because the driver named no advisory evidence ID, POL-RD-13(1) makes the absent artifact a gap in the bundle rather than an exculpatory clause invoked against a cited artifact, so POL-RD-10(5) is not engaged and the case should be resolved on the trace arithmetic rather than held for human review. The driver's congestion account is not contradicted by anything on file: the trace shows a 40-minute, 23.97 km run whose distinct speeds top out at 62.0 km/h, averaging about 36 km/h, which is consistent with the contemporaneous in-app message that the AYE was jammed.

Each draft's own explanation

Short version: the route deviation is real and established, no excuse for it survives on this record, and the fare arithmetic gives the rider SGD 13.70 back out of the SGD 58.10 charged. THE DEVIATION. POL-RD-01 makes the GPS trace the governing measurement, and the trace records 23.97 km between the recorded pickup and dropoff. Optimum is 18.0 km, so the excess is 5.97 km, or 33.2% of optimal. Both establishment tests are met (above 20% and above 0.8 km), so the deviation is ESTABLISHED. It is not a MATERIAL deviation — it is under both the 50% and 8.0 km gates — so POL-RD-06 does not engage. To the rider: the 24.0 km on the trip record is a rounded copy and the trace's 23.97 km is used; your 'extra 6 km' is a slight overstatement, and the measured excess is 5.97 km. NO EXONERATION. To the driver: your congestion account cannot be run under POL-RD-03, because that clause needs a traffic_advisory naming a road the optimal route uses with a validity window covering the trip, and the only advisory artifact in the bundle, EV-ADVIS-00114-01, is MISSING with weight 0.0 and no payload. Under POL-RD-13 the assertion is tested against that advisory and nothing else, so it carries no weight under POL-RD-08 and neither reduces the 5.97 km nor supplies an amended optimal route. Your in-app message at 18:59:20 ('AYE jam boss, this way faster') records only that you chose to leave the optimal corridor; your counterparty statement that there was 'No advisory that I know of' is consistent with that. Because you named no advisory evidence ID, POL-RD-13(1) makes the absent artifact a gap in the bundle rather than an exculpatory clause invoked against a cited artifact, so POL-RD-10(5) is not engaged and this case is ruleable now rather than held. For completeness: tracing speed against a jam is not a substitute for the advisory the clause requires. To the rider: POL-RD-04 does not apply either. Your message at 18:58:40 ('adam road?? jurong is the other way') is a challenge, not an instruction to detour, and no chat message carries a waypoint_hint, so no distance is excluded from the excess on that ground. Neither side gets an adjusted optimal: the booked 18.0 km stands. THE REFUND (POL-RD-02, METERED fare on EV-FARE-00114). recomputed_fare = ((3.80 base + 0.75 x 18.0 km + 0.28 x 30.0 min) x 1.6 surge) + 0.80 platform fee + 2.50 ERP on the optimal route = (25.70 x 1.6) + 3.30 = 41.12 + 3.30 = 44.42. Refund = 58.10 charged_total - 44.42 = 13.68, rounded up to the nearest SGD 0.05 on the payable figure = SGD 13.70. The 1.6 surge is read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier and is preserved on both sides of the equation; the surge you accepted is not refunded, only the distance and time over the excess. ERP. Of the 4.50 charged, 2.50 is the Kim Keat Link gantry on the optimal route and stays inside the recomputed fare. The 2.00 Adam Road gantry is off the optimal route but is a genuine crossing — the trace passes 8.76 m from it — so it is not a phantom line and no billing-integrity referral arises. Under POL-RD-09(1) it is already comprehended in the 13.70 and must not be added on top of it. OUTCOME. PARTIAL_REFUND of SGD 13.70 to the rider; no driver compensation. 13.70 is above the SGD 0.50 de minimis and well under the 90% of charged_total that would make it a full refund. No referral fires: no material deviation, no repeat-pattern threshold (deviation_flags_90d is 1 across 412 completed 90-day trips, under both the count and ratio gates), and no unmatched charge line. Confidence is 0.9; the facts the ruling rests on — the trace measurement, the booked optimal and the fare lines — all sit on weight-1.0 artifacts, and the missing advisory carries no fact and does not cap the ruling. The monetary effect (13.70) exceeds the SGD 8.00 automatic-execution threshold, so the amount is issued but held for human release under POL-GEN-05.

ESCALATION. No POL-RD-10 trigger fires. OUTCOME. PARTIAL_REFUND of SGD 13.70 to the rider, against the SGD 15.00 contested. Confidence 0.90, capped at 1.0 by the weight-1.0 artifacts that carry the deciding facts (EV-GPS-00114, EV-TRIP-00114, EV-FARE-00114); the missing advisory carries no fact and does not drag the cap. To both parties. This was the Friday 7 Aug 2026 Bugis–Jurong East trip TRP-00114. The platform's booked optimal route is 18.0 km (EV-TRIP-00114). The trip's own GPS trace (EV-GPS-00114, 241 fixes, 10 s sampling, 100% coverage, max_gap_sec 0.0) runs 23.97 km between the recorded pickup and dropoff — an excess of 5.97 km, or 33.17% of optimal. The trace figure governs for the threshold test under POL-RD-01, not the rounded 24.0 km copy on the trip record. Both establishment gates are cleared (over 20% and over 0.8 km), so the deviation is ESTABLISHED; it does not reach the 50% / 8.0 km materiality gates, so POL-RD-06 is not engaged and no driver-conduct referral arises. I also checked the only two profile counters POL-RD-06 permits — driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 1 (below 3) and 1/412 is 0.0024 (below 0.05) — so no repeat pattern is found; the lifetime counter prior_deviation_flags is context only and was not used as a ground. The driver's account of congestion on the AYE is tied to no artifact: EV-ADVIS-00114-01 is MISSING (weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT). Under POL-RD-13 and POL-RD-08 that external-cause assertion carries no weight, and because the driver cited no advisory identifier this is a gap in the bundle rather than an exculpatory clause invoked against a cited artifact, so POL-RD-10(5) does not fire; POL-RD-03 is simply unavailable. No rider detour request exists (the chat's only rider message is a challenge to the route, with no waypoint_hint), so no distance is excluded. Because the fare model is METERED, the remedy is arithmetic under POL-RD-02, using the 1.6 surge read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier (EV-FARE-00114) and the 2.50 ERP of the on-optimal-route Kim Keat Link gantry: recomputed_fare = (3.80 base + 0.75 x 18.0 km + 0.28 x 30.0 min) x 1.6 + 0.80 platform fee + 2.50 ERP = 44.42. Refund = 58.10 charged_total - 44.42 = 13.68, rounded up on the payable figure to 13.70. That is well above the 0.50 de minimis and only 23.5% of the charge, so it is a partial refund, not a full one. On the ERP lines: both billed gantries were genuinely crossed (the trace passes 0.0 m from Kim Keat Link and 8.76 m from Adam Road, inside the 250 m match), so neither is a phantom charge and no POL-RD-09(4) referral arises; the 2.00 Adam Road gantry is off the optimal route and is already comprehended inside the 13.70, itemised for transparency but never added on top. Confidence is 0.90: every artifact carrying the deciding facts (trace, trip record, fare breakdown) sits at weight 1.0, so the POL-GEN-02(2) cap is 1.0. The refund of 13.70 exceeds the SGD 8.00 execution threshold, so it is issued but the amount is held for a human reviewer to release.
